EVIDENCE FOR THE DEFERRED PRICING DECISION, which is exactly what you said accounting-first would
buy. Measured, not argued. This is NOT a candidate and changes nothing; c428396 is unaffected and
still awaiting review.

You deferred option (A) - stop imputing, let an abstained semantic go absent - on the grounds that
it contradicts a documented decision and moves numbers, and that once imputation is countable the
question becomes answerable. It is now countable, so I counted it.

SETUP, and its limits stated first: Anna fixture, every cell, provider abstaining on EVERY pair.
That is an upper bound, not a realistic channel - a real embedder abstains on some pairs, not all -
so read these as "how far can this move", not "how far will it".

  cells (non-excluded)                32
  cells imputing Semantic             32
  (A) vs (B) relative move in total   mean 22.28%, max 100.00%

THE MAX IS NOT A ROUNDING ARTEFACT AND IT IS THE FINDING. The worst cell:

  u2 -> Situation(e5-find)
  terms = {Propositional 0.0, Entity 0.0, Granularity 0.0, Distortion 0.0, Semantic 0.5}
  functionPrior = 0.0
  (B) total = 0.5234375      (A) total = 0.0

Under (A) that cell costs EXACTLY ZERO. The four other terms genuinely measured 0.0 - same
predicate, names matching in role, right granularity, faithful mode - so they are real perfect
agreement. The one dimension nobody could measure was the highest-weighted one. Dropping its
imputation leaves a cost of zero, which is not merely "cheap": zero is the floor, so this becomes
the best anchor available anywhere in the space, BECAUSE its semantic distance is unknown.

SO OPTION (A) IS NOT SIMPLY THE HONEST OPTION. Naively implemented it converts "we could not measure
the semantic distance" into "this is a flawless match" - the same defect class this entire bead is
about, appearing inside the proposed remedy. It is the partial-evidence version of the failure that
Exclusion.Unassessable exists to prevent: there the cell measured nothing and would have won on the
function prior; here the cell measured four zeros and wins on their absence of contradiction.

WHAT THAT IMPLIES FOR THE EVENTUAL RULING, offered as options rather than a lean, because I have
been wrong once today about which way an argument cuts:
  - (B) as shipped: keep the neutral price, and the receipt now says when it was used. No failure
    mode of this kind, at the cost of a price that is a convention rather than a measurement.
  - (A) plus a floor: absent semantic makes the cell ineligible to win outright - the Unassessable
    treatment extended from "measured nothing" to "measured nothing that discriminates".
  - (A) plain: rejected by the evidence above unless someone wants unknown-semantic cells to be
    preferentially selected.

I am not proposing any of them now. The number you asked for is 22.28% mean movement with a
zero-cost worst case, and the worst case is the part that decides it.

A CORRECTION INSIDE MY OWN MEASUREMENT, since it bears on trusting the figures. My first run
reported mean 10.05% because I reconstructed the eligible set as terms ++ missingTerms. That is
wrong: Chart and Structural are RECORDED missing on this fixture but were never ELIGIBLE, because
the view carries no charts. Using the union inflates wEligible and understates the move. That is the
same confusion between "absent" and "impossible" that this bead is about, committed by me inside the
probe measuring it, two hours after fixing the identical confusion in chartEligible. I caught it
because the max of exactly 1.0000 looked too round to be real, not because I re-read my own code.
Corrected figure is 22.28%.
